info.name: OAN Authentication Service API
info.description:
JWT authentication and user lifecycle service for OpenAgriNet (OAN). Provides RESTful endpoints for user registration, login, token refresh, logout, password recovery, identity introspection, metadata aggregation, and admin user and role management.

Generated from openapi/openapi_v1.yaml by postman/generate_postman_collection.py; do not edit by hand.

Import oan_auth_environment.json and set base_url, admin_username and admin_password. Every other variable is generated when blank. Run the collection top to bottom: Register and Login store the tokens protected requests use; the Admin folder signs in as the admin itself, and Onboard a user stores target_user_id for the rest. Reset Password is skipped unless reset_key is set, because that key only arrives by email.

request.description: Send exactly one credential. `refresh_token` (this app's session): exchanged for a new access token and rotated refresh token. `access_token` (an IAM session, expired token accepted): its issuer picks the IAM, which refreshes from the forwarded IAM cookies (`<cookie_prefix>X-Access-Token`, `X-ID-Token`, `X-Session-Id`); relay every `Set-Cookie` of the response to the browser unchanged, they carry the new tokens. The IAM answer is `refreshed: true` when a new access token was issued, `false` when the current one is still valid. Session over: 401, log the user out. IAM unreachable: 503, keep the session and retry.

request.description: Send exactly one credential. `refresh_token` (this app's session): revoked; access tokens expire on their own. `access_token` (an IAM session, expired token accepted): its issuer picks the IAM; forward that IAM's cookies (`<cookie_prefix>X-Access-Token`, `X-ID-Token`, `X-Session-Id`) and relay every `Set-Cookie` of the response, they clear IAM's cookies. `provider_logout: true` means the identity provider session was ended too; otherwise, when `logout_url` is present, send the browser there to end it.

Also returns the option's `cookie_prefix`: after the IAM callback, the access token is in the `<cookie_prefix>X-Access-Token` cookie.
